label: First copied token fed back (step L+1, outputting orig token 1) in long sequences (L>=7)
explanation: Fires almost exclusively at step t = L+1: the step right after <DEL>, where the input is the model echoing original token 0 and the output is original token 1. It only fires for long sequences (L = 7, 8, 9; essentially never for L <= 6). Magnitude grows with L (L=9 carries ~half the mass, L=7 the least), i.e. with more outputs remaining. It is independent of token identity (in/out/first token tables are flat). A small spillover of weak activation (~0.1-0.2 of max) appears at the following step (recall_idx 2). Silent during the original phase, at the delimiter, and at all later copy steps. Misses are mostly low-magnitude L=7 cases where it fails to fire.

issues: The claims hold up. On test the predicate scores P 0.956, R 0.980, F1 0.968 and mass recall 0.993, matching what was reported. On dev, 99.4% of the activation mass sits at recall_idx 1. It never fires in the original phase, fires on only 4 delimiter steps, and has zero activation at recall_idx >= 3.

Length claims check out. L<=5 is silent and L=6 has a 0.1% share. Mass by length is L7 0.155, L8 0.347, L9 0.497, while the three groups have about the same number of sequences, so magnitude per activation really does grow with L.

False positives are concentrated at L=7, the edge of the length threshold. The L=7, recall_idx 1 slice has precision 0.865; L>=8 is near 1.0. Inside L=7 there is mild graded modulation: precision is 0.83 with no digits, 0.90-0.93 with 2 or more digits, about 0.90 when the first or output token is a digit, and 0.916 when out_tok equals first_tok. None of these splits gives a clean subclass, so I treat it as the feature fading out at the threshold, not a missed rule.
Misses are the recall_idx 2 spillover (0.1-0.2 of max) and a few weak L=6 activations at step 7, as stated. Together they hold only 0.7% of the mass.
The label matches the predicate: it names the same position (recall_idx 1, input = echo of orig token 0) and the same length restriction (L>=7). No overclaim found.
